claims.claim: ⚠️ **Onset is usually rapid, with potentially fatal neurological and cardiovascular effects** — but toxicity can appear later after oral or topical use.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Management is largely supportive, with IV lipid emulsion in severe cases.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Methaemoglobinaemia** is more likely with benzocaine, lignocaine or prilocaine; it **does not depend on dose, and children are more prone to it, even after topical use.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Allergic reactions including anaphylaxis are possible** — treat along conventional lines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Usually therapeutic error.** ⚠️ **Fatalities are reported after ingesting lignocaine-containing local and topical preparations**, despite first-pass metabolism.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most agents have a 2-hour elimination half-life; bupivacaine's is 5 hours or longer.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maximum recommended doses (mg/kg):** ropivacaine 2.5–3 · bupivacaine 1–2.5 · prilocaine 5–7 · lignocaine 4–5 · mepivacaine 4–5. ⚠️ **Toxicity can occur below these after IV or intra-arterial injection**; larger doses can be given with adrenaline. **Bupivacaine is particularly cardiotoxic.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** any symptomatic patient · any deliberate self-poisoning · a significant accidental overdose · accidental injection into a vein or artery.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Early features:** tinnitus, difficulty focusing, dizziness, anxiety, agitation, confusion, drowsiness, perioral or tongue numbness, metallic taste.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe:** seizures, coma · bradycardia, hypotension, dysrhythmias, conduction block, collapse, asystole · respiratory depression, apnoea. **Cardiac arrest may be the first sign after massive IV overdose.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigate:** UEC, arterial blood gas, methaemoglobin; **serial ECGs for sodium channel blockade** (prolonged PR and QRS, large terminal R in aVR).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immediately stop the local anaesthetic and call for help.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any cardiotoxicity: intubate and ventilate immediately** to prevent hypoxaemia, hypercarbia and acidosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ventricular dysrhythmias: IV sodium bicarbonate 1–2 mmol/kg (max 100 mmol), repeated every 1–2 minutes until there is a perfusing rhythm**; amiodarone can be used. **AVOID calcium channel blockers, beta blockers and local anaesthetics.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Seizures: benzodiazepines. Hypotension: normal saline 20 mL/kg IV, then inotropes if needed; AVOID vasopressin.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recovery from local-anaesthetic cardiac arrest may take over 1 hour.** Decontamination is not indicated; enhanced elimination is not useful.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Methaemoglobinaemia: IV methylene blue 1–2 mg/kg, given over 5 minutes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lipid emulsion (intralipid 20%) for severe cardiovascular toxicity or cardiac arrest.** Caution with egg yolk, soya or peanut protein hypersensitivity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **20% lipid emulsion: 1.5 mL/kg IV bolus across 1 minute, followed by an infusion of 0.25 mL/kg/minute.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After 5 minutes, if collapse persists or worsens: up to 2 repeat boluses (at least 5 minutes apart) and double the infusion to 0.5 mL/kg/minute.** Continue until circulation is stable or the **max cumulative 12 mL/kg** is reached.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lipid emulsion adverse events:** allergy and anaphylaxis, laboratory interference, pancreatitis (rare), VTE (rare), pulmonary hypertension, acute lung injury, haematuria, hypertriglyceridaemia, ECMO circuit obstruction.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lignocaine teething gel or other topical ingestion: hospital assessment if over 6 mg/kg or any symptoms.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Continue care in intensive care or high dependency; consider tertiary transfer for any patient with local anaesthetic toxicity.** PIPER: 1300 137 650.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for every intentional overdose.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Local anaesthetic poisoning' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Local_anaesthetic_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
